note_sections.t: Re-evaluation for treatment decision following prior prostate cancer diagnosis and significant PSA rise to 160.0 ng/mL.

Long-standing referral for prostate cancer management. The patient is a 62-year-old retired bank clerk, married, living in a ground-floor apartment with his partner. He has a history of scrotal/inguinal surgery and is a non-smoker. He consumes 14 units of alcohol weekly and performs light weight-training at home twice a week. IPSS score is 10/35, indicating moderate lower urinary tract symptoms. Recent appointments include an audiology hearing test, orthopaedic outpatient knee follow-up, and memory clinic baseline screening. He has no active medications and reports allergies to NSAIDs. PSA trend shows a dramatic increase from 12.7 ng/mL in March 2024 to 160.0 ng/mL in February 2025.

On DRE, the prostate is enlarged with an irregular, nodular left lobe and palpable extracapsular extension, consistent with clinical stage cT3a. General examination reveals a well-nourished male with normal cardiopulmonary findings and no lymphadenopathy. Vital signs are stable with BP 131/85 mmHg and HR 75 bpm.

living: Lives in ground-floor apartment with partner
admin: Patient self-employed; flexible appointment slots requested.
